The review describes Poké Balls being consumed unusually quickly after purchase, allegedly because captures break out more often, so the player must buy more. This supports Pay to Progress because payment is presented as necessary to continue capture gameplay, and Illusion of Control because the reviewer alleges purchase-linked manipulation of capture outcomes. The edit states that the review was not written by the reviewer, which fits store-review impersonation. Intermediate Currency is rejected because Poké Balls are items, not currency; Waste Aversion and Reward Mania are not supported because no stranded currency or reward-delivery mechanic is described. Reciprocity is rejected because the reviewer denies actually talking to other players.

labels.rationale: The span describes needing to spend money on more Poké Balls to continue capture gameplay.

labels.label: P_IllusionOfControl
labels.span: since I started purchasing, items "poke" balls that when I tried to make a capture that they keep breaking out
labels.rationale: The reviewer alleges that purchasing is associated with manipulated or worse capture outcomes.

labels.label: S_FriendSpamImpersonation
labels.span: I DID NOT WRITE THIS REVIEW
labels.rationale: The edit describes a store review appearing under the player's identity without being authored by them, fitting the store-review impersonation boundary.

Fighting overpowered real players describes Competition, while the algorithm assigning mismatched opponents describes hidden matchmaking manipulation under Illusion of Control. No search is needed; other labels are not supported by a specific mechanic span.

parsed.analysis: The review describes spending money as a route through game progression in "buy their way through the game," which satisfies M_PayToProgress. The mention of hacking describes player conduct rather than a game design mechanic, so it is rejected under R2. "Nobody enjoys grinding a game anymore" is a general evaluation without a named repetitive task tied to progress, so T_Grinding is rejected under its boundary rule. Having an inventory full of useless gear does not describe stranded currency, capacity pressure, or forfeited value, so M_WasteAversion is rejected.

labels.rationale: This describes players spending money to advance through the game.

parsed.analysis: The review describes spending real money for stronger or advantageous robots, supporting M_PayToProgress. It also describes an owned robot being nerfed after a month while newer robots are introduced, supporting M_PowerCreep. The reference to clans of paying players defeating the reviewer describes player-versus-player competition, supporting S_Competition. Lag is attributed to a technical problem, so it is not coded under R11. No scarcity, gambling, collection, or appointment mechanic is described.

parsed.analysis: The review describes accumulated bag contents and coins, including purchased coins, being lost after leaving and returning. This supports P_EasyToGetHardToLose because exit causes forfeiture of held value, and T_MandatoryMarathon because stopping the session results in loss. M_IntermediateCurrency also applies because the review explicitly describes coins as purchased. M_WasteAversion and M_PayToProgress are rejected: no stranded currency shortfall or payment-for-progress gate is described.

parsed.analysis: The review describes prolonged progress-oriented grinding, purchases of Gold/Event Passes, and an update that devalues previously earned hero-equipment progress by giving equivalent progress to new players. I considered T_PlayingByAppointment and T_DailyRewards because of "playing actively every day," but no reward reset, expiry, or game-imposed schedule is described. M_PayToProgress and M_IntermediateCurrency were rejected because the review does not state that payment is required for progress or that real money is converted into currency. S_Competition was rejected because "overtake me" does not identify a competitive mode. T_InfiniteTreadmill and P_EasyToGetHardToLose were rejected because years of remaining progress does not establish endless completion or reluctance to quit. The search resolved Gold Pass and Event Pass as purchasable pass features, supporting M_RecurringFee. ([support.supercell.com](https://support.supercell.com/clash-of-clans/en/articles/events-2.html?utm_source=openai))

labels.label: T_Grinding
labels.span: After a year of grinding
labels.rationale: Explicitly describes prolonged grinding undertaken in the context of game progress.

labels.label: M_RecurringFee
labels.span: buying gold/event passes
labels.rationale: Describes purchasing pass-based monetization, an indicator of recurring-fee design.

labels.label: M_PowerCreep
labels.span: an update that invalidates most of the progress I achieved. New players get my current level of hero equipment progress for free, and can easily overtake me, while I get nothing and am still years away from maxing it out, despite playing actively every day and spending money on the game
labels.rationale: The update makes previously earned and paid-for progress substantially less valuable by granting equivalent progress to newer players.

parsed.analysis: The review describes purchasing in-game coins with real money: "$20 for only 100k or so coins." This satisfies M_IntermediateCurrency because real money is exchanged for virtual currency. The poor prize value does not itself describe a codable mechanic under R2. M_Gambling is rejected because the review does not clearly describe paying to participate in a chance-based reward mechanic; M_PayToProgress is rejected because the purchase is not explicitly tied to progressing; M_WasteAversion is rejected because no stranded currency, capacity limit, or specific shortfall is described; and P_RewardMania is rejected because the complaint concerns prize value rather than reward delivery.

labels.label: M_IntermediateCurrency

labels.rationale: The span describes exchanging real-world money for in-game coins.
